qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: General construction contracting is an inherently commoditized, tender-driven service business characterized by low operating margins (~3.5%) and fixed-price contract overrun risks. Commercial property development is capital-intensive and highly cyclical, suffering sharp writedowns during real estate downturns. The company lacks structural pricing power and fails to achieve a 12% multi-cycle GAAP ROIC.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3 (3a=None, 3b=N, REJECT). Skanska operates as a general construction contractor and commercial property developer in the Nordics, Europe, and the US. Construction contracting is a tender-driven commodity business with thin operating margins (~3.5%), while commercial property development is cyclical with periodic portfolio impairments, failing the 12% multi-cycle ROIC moat threshold.
qualitative.evidence: Construction operating margins consistently hovered around ~3.3-3.5% between 2020 and 2024. Commercial Property Development ROCE collapsed to 2.6% in 2024 and was negative in 2023 due to commercial real estate devaluations in the US and Europe. Consolidated through-cycle ROIC falls well short of the 12% hurdle.
